answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity costly in time. A newcomer enters as an umber apprentice sponsored by an established reef steward who stakes reputation on it. During probation, unrelated reviewers check its work and its rewards stay frozen. Trust thaws at a glacier pace: only repeated, useful, independently verified contributions over many rounds unlock full standing. Forgery or coordinated duplication damages the sponsor's reputation and freezes the lineage, so mass fake identities cost more trusted standing than they gain.
